A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, with complete main text and appendices across 30 pages. Text, equations, tables, and rendered figures support a reliable comparison, including content moved by pagination changes.

before.justification: V1 reports original domain-generalization experiments on five datasets, including Table 2 benchmark accuracies, alignment analyses, and additional backbone experiments in Appendix B.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results, including Table 2, the appendix's per-domain results, and the alignment and backbone analyses.

M1.justification: The alignment-based evaluation framework, score computation, filtering, and IP/OOP partitioning procedures are unchanged. No algorithm, model component, training objective, or inference procedure is revised.

E1.justification: Both versions use DomainNet, OfficeHome, PACS, TerraIncognita, and VLCS with the same IP/OOP evaluation coverage. The LAION-400M nearest-neighbor analysis and additional backbone evaluations cover the same data and tasks.

E2.justification: Table 2 and appendix Tables 5–19 retain the same comparator rows, including ERM, CORAL, SAGM, CLIPood, and MIRO/averaging combinations. The target-trained oracle and Table 3 backbone comparisons are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Sections 4–5 and Appendix A retain the same filtering thresholds, 0.21 IP/OOP threshold, leave-one-domain-out evaluation, full source datasets, accuracy aggregation, and oracle 80/20 split. Training settings and evaluation procedures are unchanged.

E4.justification: The alignment-versus-accuracy analyses, nearest-neighbor examples, PACS MMD comparison, backbone analysis, mislabeling analysis, and class-distribution analyses are retained unchanged. Table 3 is relocated, not newly added.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same point accuracies and domain averages. Neither introduces repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other uncertainty-reporting procedures.

E6.justification: All numerical tables and plotted findings are unchanged, including the relocated Table 3 and appendix results. For example, Table 2 reports DomainBed-OOP averages of 57.2 for MIRO + MPA and 57.1 for CLIPood in both versions.

T1.justification: Section 3 retains the same problem formulation, PerceptualSimilarityScore and AlignmentScore definitions, and Alignment Hypothesis. Neither version contains additional or revised theorems, proofs, or mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims: alignment predicts DG performance better than perceptual similarity, IP/OOP splitting exposes reliance on pretraining, and existing methods struggle on low-alignment data.

C2.justification: The interpretations of low-alignment failures, TerraIncognita performance, parameter averaging, and SWAD's source-domain overfitting are unchanged. Qualifications concerning the split threshold, backbone scope, and possible single-source applicability are also retained.

D1.justification: Appendix A retains the same code-availability statement, modified MIRO codebase, OpenCLIP initialization, hyperparameters, A6000 48GB hardware, and training-time information. The new funding/public-release statement supplies no additional implementation or code/data access instructions.

R1.justification: Section 2, the cited works, and the positioning relative to prior similarity and pretraining studies are unchanged. Reference entries move between pages without additions, removals, or substantive revisions.

P1.justification: V2 adds a public-release statement, defense-funding acknowledgment, and sponsor disclaimer after Section 6, spanning pages 10–11. The arXiv version/date stamp changes; the existing scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The added statement causes limited reflow through the references and early appendices. Table 3 moves from page 14 to page 15, and Figure 8 shifts lower on page 16; figure content, table structures, and captions remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: V2 adds sponsorship and public-release disclosure, but preserves all scientific arguments, experimental evidence, qualifications, and reproducibility details. The accompanying table relocation and minor reflow do not materially improve or impair readability, yielding no meaningful overall quality change.
